headline: Recommended approval of a City Manager update on Spectrum cable contract talks and recommended filing a WRTA bus route removal order.
summary: The meeting covered the removal of a bus route that passes the EcoTarium and the state of negotiations for a new cable contract with Spectrum. The committee recommended filing the bus route item and recommended approval of the cable contract item, each by a 3-0 roll call vote.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the July 23, 2026 meeting by a 3-0 roll call vote.
Recommended filing the order on the removal of a bus route that passes the EcoTarium, 222 Harrington Way, by a 3-0 roll call vote.
Recommended approval of the order asking the City Manager to update Council on the Spectrum cable contract negotiations, by a 3-0 roll call vote.

. Miscellaneous Items 3 
September 17, 2026 Page 2 of 5Public Service and Transportation Committee
Report of the Committee on Public Service and Transportation Upon the Order of 
Councilor Morris A. Bergman and Councilor Candy Mero -Carlson - Request Standing 
Committee on Public Service and Transportation Committee hold a public discussion 
with the WRTA Administrator relative to the removal of a bus route that passes the 
EcoTarium, 222 Harrington Way.
# 11d CC January 27, 2026
a.
Chairperson Councilor Bilotta read the item and recognized the WRTA Administrator, who 
provided an overview and future plans related to the bus route that passes the EcoTarium, 222 
Harrington Way.
Chairperson Councilor Bilotta recognized Councilor Fresolo, who discussed the removal of a bus 
stop on Waverly St. with the Commissioner of Transportation and Mobility.
Chairperson Councilor Bilotta then discussed public outreach efforts made by the WRTA when 
relocating bus stops, how public meetings are organized, as well as the timeline associated with the 
microtransit module study in the city with the WRTA Administrator.
Chairperson Councilor Bilotta recognized the Commissioner of Transportation and Mobility, who 
discussed the department’s collaboration efforts with the WRTA related to the Mobility Action 
Plan.
Chairperson Councilor Bilotta moved for a roll call vote to recommend the item be filed.
Recommend File on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays
September 17, 2026 Page 3 of 5Public Service and Transportation Committee
Order of Councilor Gary Rosen - Request City Manager provide City Council with an 
update concerning the current state of negotiations for a new cable contract with 
Spectrum. The previous agreement, which expired in October 2023, was marred by 
Spectrum's contract violations, poor customer service, poor cable reliability and failure 
to provide contractual senior discounts, among others.
# 13d CC February 24, 2026
b.
Chairperson Councilor Bilotta read the item and recognized the Director of Cable Services, who 
provided an overview of the item.
Chairperson Councilor Bilotta recognized Councilor Fresolo, who discussed the role of the 
Director of Cable Services in the contract negotiations with Charter Communications /Spectrum, 
challenges related to setting programming rates with cable companies and senior discount 
negotiations with the Director of Cable Services.
Chairperson Councilor Bilotta then discussed details associated with the sources and distribution 
of the Public, Educational, and Government (PEG) funding with the Director of Cable Services.
Chairperson Councilor Bilotta recognized Councilor Ojeda, who discussed the senior discount 
agreement with Charter Communications /Spectrum including how much is owed by the company 
to senior subscribers in the city with the Director of Cable Services.
Chairperson Councilor Bilotta then discussed the feasibility of calculating the senior discount 
amount that is owed by Charter Communications /Spectrum, challenges related to budget cuts due 
to decreasing PEG funding and considerations regarding inclusion of streaming services with PEG 
funding with the Director of Cable Services.
Chairperson Councilor Bilotta recognized Councilor Ojeda, who discussed the decrease in number 
of cable subscribers with the Director of Cable Services.
Chairperson Councilor Bilotta recognized the WCCA TV Executive Director, who discussed the 
importance of creating new legislations to increase PEG funding, challenges related to budget cuts 
and current legislations under consideration to modernize PEG funding at the State level.
Chairperson Councilor Bilotta brought forth the following Chairman’s Order: Request City 
Manager work with the Worcester Chamber of Commerce to explore principal sponsorships for 
WCCA TV.
Chairperson Councilor Bilotta moved for a roll call vote to recommend the item be approved. 
Recommend Approval on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays
